newsitem.title: USA: Florida student charged with slipping teacher LSD.
newsitem.headline: Florida student charged with slipping teacher LSD.

text.p: A Florida teenager was in custody on Sunday charged with spiking his teacher's drink with the hallucinogen LSD, police said.
Andrew Lewis, 17, faced two felony changes of poisoning and delivering drugs within 1,000 feet of a school, said Gary Davidson, spokesman for the Volusia County Sheriff's Office.
Investigators were considering charges against two other students who may have been accomplices in helping hide the rest of the LSD Lewis took to school, the spokesman said.

The incident took place last Wednesday, when several students watched as Lewis, a senior, pulled out a piece of paper, tore off a square and dropped it into a soda bottle on teacher Linda Woodard's desk while she was out of the classroom, police said.
"Everyone knew it was LSD," said Jenny Kelly, a student president in the classroom at the time. "He told us it was LSD. He said he was on LSD himself."

Woodard returned and drank some of the soda before any of the students warned her. She was treated briefly at a local hospital, where a blood sample was taken for testing, but apparently suffered no harm from the incident.

On Friday evening, a blood test for Woodard came back positive for LSD and an arrest warrant was issued for Lewis. He appeared before a county judge on Saturday who refused to release him from a juvenile detention facility.
